record.title: The expressivity hierarchy conjecture for finitely iterated supervenience languages
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{L}_{\Rrightarrow^n}$ be the propositional language with the $n$-ary supervenience operator $\Rrightarrow^n$.

**Expressivity hierarchy conjecture.** For all $n\in\mathbb{N}$, $\mathcal{L}_{\Rrightarrow^{n+1}}$ is more expressive than $\mathcal{L}_{\Rrightarrow^n}$.

The paper establishes the corresponding result for $n=0$ and leaves the generalization to future work.

source_review.recovered_scope: Form n has atoms, negation, conjunction and an n+1-ary dependence connective. At w it quantifies over u,v with S(w,u,v), agreement on all n antecedents implying agreement on consequent. Arbitrary ternary frames, not only complete successor relations.
source_review.depth: Relevant primary definitions and claim passages inspected; specific proof-body reads stated in route. No entire-literature review.

record.mathematical_attempts_and_gap: Complete syntax translation Form 2 -> Form 1 and semantics theorem. Gate(A,B):=A => (A and B) tests agreement on B among A-world pairs. Four Boolean cells for antecedents A,C express binary dependence. Structural induction handles nested modalities. Therefore strictness at n=1 is false.
